svg.title: Cloud Health Office blueprint architecture on Google Cloud
svg.desc: Members, providers, phone platforms, trading partners, other plans and the state connect through CMS-0057-F FHIR APIs (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, Provider Directory, CRD, DTR, PAS, SMART, Bulk export) and X12 EDI (270/271, 276/277, 834, 837, 999, 835, 837 encounters, 820, 278 import). Behind them, twelve plan operations modules run in one tenant: member service and call tracking, appeals and grievances, utilization management and prior authorization, care management, enrollment and eligibility, provider management, benefit plan management, claims adjudication, fee schedules and pricing, payment and capitation with 835, accounts receivable, and premium billing. An advisory AI layer suggests EDI fixes and reviews pended claims with PHI redaction and human decisions. The current core feeds a daily file drop into the tenant's data, which can be exported as CPCDS. All of it sits on a Google Cloud security foundation; items marked dashed are configured or built per plan.
svg.text: Cloud Health Office blueprint: everything a health plan runs, in one tenant on Google Cloud
Each plan gets its own tenant in its own Google Cloud project. Start with the daily file drop beside your current core, then move one function at a time.
FRONT DOOR: STANDARD APIS AND EDI
PLAN OPERATIONS: ONE PLATFORM, ONE TENANT
Every call, chat or email logged;
opens cases with the right clock
Also in the platform: correspondence, ID cards, member documents, work queues, encounter submission, risk adjustment, terminology.
DATA: START BESIDE YOUR CORE, KEEP A COPY YOU OWN
Claims, members, authorizations, providers and FHIR stores;
event streams; documents; shadow adjudication results;
CPCDS export, so the data can always leave with you
Tenant taken only from a validated token
One project per plan, org policies
Solid outline: in the repository today. Dashed amber: configured or built per plan at deployment. HIPAA posture and BAA approach are drafted; SOC 2 is planned.
